dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Ah, my daughter has fled the country for some time now. I wonder how she's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Eh, you're going on about that again, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: How could you say that? I don't even know if she is getting by or not. I wonder if she's alright...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Didn't I tell you that someone saw her in Liyue? Just stop talking about it already.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: I know, I know. But not having seen her in person, I'm still worried...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Just relax. She'll be okay. She is our daughter, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Our daughter has been independent since she was little. She knows how to take care of herself. She started cooking for herself at the age of seven or eight. Why, by the time she was a teenager, she could already sail out to sea by herself.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She enjoys being free and traveling around. She must have been really unhappy at being trapped in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Trust me, she'll be fine. She is out of the country, living a free and happy life. She's probably made new friends already.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She most likely doesn't write letters to us because she doesn't want the government to find out and bring us trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Yes, that must be it...

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Ah, my daughter has fled the country for some time now. I wonder how she's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Now, now, didn't our daughter say so in her letter? She's doing well! We don't have to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: But... She might've been fine when she wrote this letter, but how can we be sure that she didn't encounter any trouble afterward?

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Not having seen her in person, I can't help but be worried...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Just relax. She'll be okay. She is our daughter, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Our daughter has been independent since she was little. She knows how to take care of herself. She started cooking for herself at the age of seven or eight. Why, by the time she was a teenager, she could already sail out to sea by herself.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She enjoys being free and traveling around. She must have been really unhappy at being trapped in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Trust me, she'll be fine. She is out of the country, living a free and happy life. She's probably made new friends already.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Whenever you think of her, take her letter out and read it again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: If our daughter knew how much you worry about her every day, she would be troubled, too.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: After waiting for so long, our daughter has finally returned home!

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Well, you look happy.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Our daughter has returned! Of course I, her mother, am happy! Aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Of course I am! But you need to stop pulling her aside to tell her all sorts of things. She'll get sick of it!

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: ...Atsuko's been gone so long... There's so much I want to talk to her about.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Well, keep talking, then. I mean, what's the worst that could happen? That she might leave once she tires of your yakking?

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Hah! Don't you try to scare me. I've already thought all this through.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Since she likes exploring so much, we should just let her — all I ask is that she sends us letters to tell us how she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: I mean, it will still get a little lonely when she's not around...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Come on, you'll still have me!

dialogues.speaker: Michiru
dialogues.text: Hah, as if that's the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Youngster, are you also away from your parents and traveling abroad?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: My daughter would be about your age. She's also alone and abroad...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May I ask about your daughter?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: My daughter's name is Atsuko. She left home to seek freedom and hasn't returned yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She's been a tough girl since she was young, longing for a free and independent life. Ever since the Sakoku Decree took effect, she became more and more unhappy. I just knew that she would leave, and she did eventually do so...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Although I know what my daughter is capable of, I'm still worried about her as her father...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: See you. I really hope that I can see my baby girl soon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've met someone by that name in Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: R—Really? Is she about this tall, with short hair?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Ahh, excellent. Excellent! If it really is her, I should really thank the Liyue adepti for protecting her...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Oh no, I should thank you, too. Thank you for bringing us news of her.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Wonderful! Absolutely wonderful...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, Traveler. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Since you're traveling alone, please watch out for your own safety...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about your daughter...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: My daughter Atsuko has been a free-spirited girl since she was young. Ever since the Sakoku Decree took effect, she became more and more unhappy.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Soon, she left us and started traveling abroad.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: However, Atsuko came home just a while back.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Her mother and I were so happy during those few days. The girl we were looking forward to seeing finally came back. It was like a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Sadly, she didn't stay long before leaving. She probably left to travel some more.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Our girl is all grown up now. She has her own view of the world. Guess we can't keep her here forever...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the letter...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: You mean that letter? It almost caused a misunderstanding back then, and I apologize for that.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: After our daughter left again, that letter constantly reminds me and her mother of her.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: I often take it out and read it. Thank you so much for bringing the letter to us. Thank you, truly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Goodbye. I really hope that I can see my little girl soon...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, Traveler. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Since you're traveling alone, please watch out for your own safety...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: That's good, that's good. Every time I look at you, I'm reminded of our Atsuko.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She's definitely settled down a lot, and she's far better at doing the household chores as well.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: She doesn't want to tell us much about it, but I can guess that she's had her fair share of hardships out there.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: You don't seem that old yourself, Traveler, and yet you're always out abroad...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: I know that you're no ordinary person... but still, do be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Make more friends while you're out there, sure, but be sure to keep your eyes watchful. You'll avoid coming to grief that way.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Hah, look at me nagging at you. Just like our girl's mother!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Goodbye, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's talk about Atsuko...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Ah, Atsuko. She's never been one for restrictions.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: That she loves to roam was something that I had expected. But still, I suppose worrying is a parent's natural reaction.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: There's just nothing for it, you know? Our girl is all grown up now. She has her own way of seeing the world.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: ...Honestly, I think it's good for her. I'll be fine so long as she writes us from time to time just to let us know she's safe.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: And if she can come back to see us often like she's doing now? That would be a bonus.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the other "Atsuko"...

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Ah yes, speaking of that... That was certainly a strange incident. When Atsuko came back, she told us that the "Atsuko" who had returned home previously wasn't her.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: That other girl certainly was a bit different from our daughter, but you know what? Other than her unusually large appetite, "she" was a nice girl.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: It's just too bad that "she" left in such a hurry. I didn't have time to thank her at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: It must have been hard work bringing back all those fruits and seeds every day while she was staying with us.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: I wonder if "she" and Atsuko will ever have an opportunity to meet...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Thank you for the effort that you put in to bring this letter to us. Please accept this charm as a token of gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: When I look at you, I'm reminded of Atsuko... May the Electro Archon protect you in your journeys ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: You're welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Thank you for having brought that letter to us from so far away. It can't have been easy.

dialogues.speaker: Yoh
dialogues.text: Please, take this talisman with you. May the Great Narukami watch over your steps.
